about.text: Red Leicester is an English cheese similar to Cheddar cheese, but crumbly in texture. It is typically aged 6 to 12 months. The rind is reddish-orange with a powdery mould on it. Since the 18th century, it has been coloured orange by the addition of annatto extract during manufacture. It is a cow's milk cheese, and is named after the city of Leicester, or the ceremonial county it is located in, Leicestershire.

how.label: colour with annatto
how.text: Annatto added during making turns the paste deep orange. Traditional wheels are firm, dry and friable, while block cheeses from creameries are moister and creamier.
